title: Render Light Names | Clo 2025 Features Deep Dive

summary: ```markdown # Render Light Names | Clo 2025 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I'm going to show you this really great feature that we've added into the Clo software called naming render lights. It's going to be really useful and really helpful for a lot of your workflows. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Accessing the Render Window Okay, so here I have my garment. I'm ready, and I'm in the render window and everything. Just a quick reminder on how to get into the render window: it's through **Render** and then **Render**. So, render at the very top of your toolbar, and you just hit render, and this will open up. ## Setting Up Your 3D Window Right now, this is just a best practice that I'm going to share with you. Normally, what I do is I set up how I like it in my 3D window and how I like it in the render, and then I'll hit this lock button to lock the camera. After that, I go and open up my custom views. ### Opening Custom Views If you don't know how to open up custom views, it's simple: right-click on the empty space in the 3D window and select **Custom View**. Just make sure you're not right-clicking on the avatar or garment or anything. After that, I'll hit this little camera button to take a picture of this custom view. This way, I can work inside my 3D window. When I've hit this lock camera, it's locked to how I like it in the render. It will always update with a render if I have my interactive button on. ## Working with Lights Now, I can see everything. So, what I’m going to do is zoom out, and because I’ve locked this, it stays exactly so. You can see I have quite a few different lights here to make sure that I can keep track of all the different lights and what they're meant to be. I'm trying to go for a beachy feel where the sun's setting, but there's a soft light behind her, and there's the direct sun setting coming at you. She's very much in the moment, so that's what I'm trying to achieve. ### Locating Lights in the Render Toolbar In case I need to move my lights around or change anything, I need to know which light switch I can go and find my lighting here in my render toolbar. Here in **Render**, all the way down, there's a little light icon I can select that will show me all of the lights in my window. This is also where I can control if I want to view or hide the lights. If right now these are all active in both my 3D and my render toolbar, I can go and find my lighting here in my render toolbar. If I want to deactivate them, I can do so. This means it's active in my render and showing in my 3D. If I don't want to see it in 3D, I can just hide it. If I don't want it active in my render, I can hide it as well. ## Using Interactive Render I'm going to turn on interactive render just so you can see all of these changes in real time. If I deactivate a light, you can see here that the light gets deactivated. Same with this one; you’re starting to see the lights changing. I can click them again, and they will be reactivated. ## Naming Lights for Better Organization To help understand which light is which, right now they all just say things like directional light, rectangle light, etc., which isn't very useful. You can see right below it says **Name**, so I can just double-click here. If I need to, I can always select my light, and here I can select this light and name it "orange." Then I can select this one, double-click, hit enter, or just click away—either is fine. I can name it "danny" or something else. Now I have these names. I can also do this for another light; just double-click, zoom out, and say something like "water reflection." ### Managing Lights with Names Now, when I go back to my lights, I can actually see all of these names. So if I decide, "Hey, I wonder what it would look like if my water wasn't being reflected," I can just deactivate it and see how that would look. If I want to keep that, I can activate it again and see it. I can also say, "Oh, I wonder what would happen if I increase this?" Now I just know what every light is and why I have the placement for it. It's much easier because I see the name here. If I need to hide, lock, or delete them, I can easily do that all within this interface. ## Saving Your Work I can, of course, save all of this. I can hit save, and then all of these lights will save together. I can bring that into other project files. I can hit open, and it will come in here. ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below, and a Clo person will get back to you. Don't forget to like and subscribe! Check out our Clo YouTube channel; we've got tons of great videos. Keep having fun in Clo! ```
